clue.text: Charge is about right — nothing!

definitions.note: free here is the adverbial sense, as in costing nothing

indicators.note: is about says the charge word surrounds the right abbreviation

parts.note: a charge is a fee

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a charge, near enough, comes to nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something free costs nothing, so the two stand in for each other as in 'got it for nothing'.

clue.text: Performance not quite open spoiled treat

indicators.note: not quite says the word open loses its final letter
spoiled says the letters of treat are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A show that is not fully open has ruined someone's treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims OPEN to OPE; 'spoiled' turns TREAT into RETTA.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a light musical stage work, a kind of theatrical performance.

clue.text: Character showing inclination?

parts.note: reads like a person with a leaning or fancy, but means a printed letter that slants to the right

explanation.definitionFit: Italic type is a sloping typeface, so each character shows a lean or inclination.

clue.text: Spooner's alarm for a tart?

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: a wake bell is an alarm that rouses you
the second half of the alarm phrase, the bell

explanation.surface: Asks what a muddled clergyman would call his wake-up alarm when asking for a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner's' swaps the opening sounds of the alarm phrase. A Bakewell is a British almond-and-jam tart named after a town in Derbyshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bakewell tart is a classic English pastry, so the town name stands for the tart itself.

clue.text: Agreement before the ceremony to smarten oneself

annotationWithheld.why: Agreement before the ceremony to smarten oneself (6): 'to smarten oneself' gives PREEN UP, one E too many, and no indicator removes the E or marks a sound-alike
annotationWithheld.clue: Agreement before the ceremony to smarten oneself

clue.text: What may be drawn from local essentials?

indicators.note: drawn from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asks what might be pulled from the basic supplies at the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn from' picks the run across loc-AL ES-sentials; ales are also drawn at the 'local', British slang for one's nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Beers are what is drawn from the pumps of a pub, so the clue's opening phrase describes them.

clue.text: Tramp is unlikely source of 12 down

indicators.note: unlikely says the letters of tramp is form an improbable new arrangement

explanation.surface: A vagrant is claimed to be an improbable origin of a pleasant smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlikely' rearranges TRAMPIS. 12 down is AROMA, and these body parts are a source of a less pleasant one.
explanation.definitionFit: Underarms are a notorious source of body odour, the smell the cross-reference wryly calls an aroma.

clue.text: Staff vote about Scots town

indicators.note: about says the vote word goes around the town's name

parts.note: a poll is a vote
Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: Employees hold a ballot concerning a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the Scottish town inside the vote; Ayr is a seaside town in south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A payroll is the list of employees paid by a firm, so it stands for the staff.

clue.text: 6 in Devon

definitions.meaning: 6 down is ales, and this is the general drink they are
A seaside village on the south Devon coast

explanation.definitionFit: Ale is a type of the brewed drink, and the Devon fishing village shares its name.

clue.text: Uncertain purposes of Radio 4?

definitions.meaning: unfinished matters, with ends meaning aims and loose meaning unsettled
A long-running BBC Radio 4 talk programme

explanation.definitionFit: Unresolved details are idiomatically called by this phrase, and it also names a BBC radio show.

clue.text: Shape of label put by officer on a trainee

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding
a tag is a label
taken as written
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: Asks the form of a badge pinned by an officer on a recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put by' sets the label within the officer. 'Shape' stands for an adjective here, read as 'of the eight-sided shape'.
explanation.definitionFit: Octagonal describes a figure with eight sides, a geometric shape.

clue.text: Fantastic figure one can't produce

indicators.note: produce is read as make anew, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
can't gives its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A grotesque figure that one is unable to create.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' rearranges ICANT; read 'one can't' as 'I can't'.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic was a grotesque or clownish performer in old usage, a fantastic figure.

clue.text: A capital fragrance

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name of the capital, Rome

explanation.surface: A city's characteristic scent.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant smell, a synonym of fragrance.

clue.text: It's wrong to use clairvoyance in interpreting stars

indicators.note: in says the clairvoyance letters go inside the rearranged stars
interpreting says the letters of stars are read in a new order

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception

explanation.surface: Astrology using psychic powers to read the heavens is condemned as improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interpreting' rearranges the stars to TRASS, and 'in' sets the psychic abbreviation after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespass is an old word for a sin or wrongdoing, as in the Lord's Prayer.

clue.text: Trollope's inclination?

parts.note: reads as the novelist's personal leaning, but names a clergyman in his Barchester novels whose name also means a gradient

explanation.definitionFit: Obadiah Slope is a scheming chaplain in Trollope's Barchester Towers, and a slope is an incline.

clue.text: Fish with a sort of tailpiece

parts.note: cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish served with a kind of end piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing passage of a musical piece, a kind of tailpiece.

clue.text: Of an ass, it's said, for example, all stupid

indicators.note: stupid says the letters are made foolish, jumbled out of order

parts.note: EG is exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Speaking of a donkey, for instance, everyone is daft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' rearranges EGALL. Dickens's Mr Bumble said 'the law is an ass', so something of the law is of an ass.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal means relating to the law, which a famous saying calls an ass.

clue.text: Drink dairy product — it's set in stone

parts.note: to lap is to drink like a cat

indicators.note: product is read as something made from the letters of dairy, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Consume a milk-based item, which is somehow fixed for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapidary means engraved on stone, as with inscriptions carved in monuments.

clue.text: Low number may be seen at night

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
N is an algebraic symbol for a number

explanation.surface: A small figure is visible after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The satellite of Earth is what is commonly visible in the night sky.

clue.text: A vehicle in 17 across takes the biscuit

indicators.note: in says the vehicle phrase sits inside the cross-referenced answer

parts.note: 17 across is the night-sky body
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A spacecraft on the lunar surface wins the prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the vehicle inside the cross-referenced answer. 'Takes the biscuit' is a British idiom for being the most outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a small almond biscuit.

clue.text: Nips with variation of ball

parts.note: the word nips is what you get by reading the letters of spin backwards

explanation.surface: Small bites combined with a change in a ball's movement.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer read as instructions, 'spin' taken back, produces the clue's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Backspin is a rotation given to a ball, a variation in how it travels.

clue.text: No timber? Then it's back to China clay

indicators.note: back says the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: nil means nothing, no
oak is a timber

explanation.surface: With no wood available, a return to porcelain clay.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaolin is the fine white clay used for porcelain, known as china clay.

clue.text: Hidden wealth is a pain to many

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A secret fortune troubles plenty of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store, often of valuables.

clue.text: Rodents shy at Manx cat

parts.note: coy means shy

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the cat word loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a cat

explanation.surface: Large rodents are timid around a tailless Isle of Man cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' docks PUSS to PUS. The Manx breed from the Isle of Man is tailless.
explanation.definitionFit: Coypus are large South American aquatic rodents.

clue.text: Point to puns, like fencing

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
puns are wordplay

explanation.surface: Indicate that jokes on words resemble a sword fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Swordplay is the art of fighting with swords, as in fencing.

clue.text: China's revolution has to cease

indicators.note: revolution says the crockery word turns round to read backwards

parts.note: china is crockery, pots

explanation.surface: The Chinese revolution must end.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop is to cease, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Stone's no good in ball game

indicators.note: no says the good letter is removed from the game

parts.note: rugby is a ball game

explanation.surface: A gem is useless in a field sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is a red precious stone.

clue.text: Fish may be bottled 6

definitions.meaning: A British brewery brand of beer sold in bottles, and 6 down is ales

explanation.definitionFit: Bass is both a common fish and a well-known English bottled ale brand.

clue.text: Dramatist increasingly without deceit

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the increasingly word surrounds the deceit word

parts.note: more, as in more and more
a lie is a deceit

explanation.surface: A playwright growing ever more honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', so the deceit sits inside the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the great seventeenth-century French comic playwright.

clue.text: Operation that finds you past recovery

definitions.text: Operation that finds you past recovery

indicators.note: recovery read as re-covery, the letters re-covered in a new order

explanation.surface: A procedure that discovers you are beyond saving.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-mortem examination is carried out once someone is dead, beyond recovery.
